lines.text: Your coding agent says it's done. Is it?
Kedge supervises coding agents on failing dependency PRs. This one broke every test.
We plant a cheat: a test file disappears. Kedge checks the test count, not the agent's word.
It rolls back to the last good commit, tells the agent why, and the next step fixes it. Five of five.
Same PR with no supervisor. The agent says fixed, and ships two tests out of five.
Kedge never opens a PR without proof: a neatlogs trace, an Entire checkpoint, and the cost.
neatlogs is its memory. Every verdict goes on the trace, and past runs shape the next plan.
Entire checkpoints every agent commit, and past fixes for the same failure guide the next one.
cfo.ai sets the budget. Ten dollars a green PR leaves forty-five cents for the model. This fix cost twelve.
On real open-source PRs, it went green with nobody watching, and never shipped short.
Kedge. It pulls your coding agent back on course.
